what: O3 source contract: the Target's ANALYTIC BEVEL REFLECTION SUPPORT, byte-anchored. The field O2's accepted reflection law is evaluated on -- rounded-rect SDF, superellipse thickness, numeric gradient, slope clamp, analytic normal, SDF rim -- plus the coordinate space and responsive law of each.
notFitted: No parameter here was chosen, adjusted or confirmed against any measured result, and in particular not against the Target's 3.3 px reflection band. Every value is read from the bundle at the recorded offset.
authorisedScope: O3 replaces ONLY the System B reflection support: the fresnel/reflection normal and the white rim mask. Refraction, dispersion, blur, geometry position and the card silhouette keep their frozen paths even where the Target derives them from this same field.

sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel space: the card's local XY multiplied by planeSize, so X and Y are world pixels on the card face and Z is the same pixel metric (the mesh scale (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1) is undone by this multiply and re-applied by `f` on the way out).
sites.responsiveScaling: planeSize = (planeWidth, planeHeight) written per frame; positionLocal.xy is the unit plane's [-0.5, +0.5], so p spans [-planeWidth/2, +planeWidth/2] x [-planeHeight/2, +planeHeight/2].
sites.whatItSettles: Every field below -- SDF, thickness, gradient, normal, rim -- is evaluated at THIS point, in plane pixels. There is no second coordinate convention in the material.

sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel space: the card's local XY multiplied by planeSize, so X and Y are world pixels on the card face and Z is the same pixel metric (the mesh scale (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1) is undone by this multiply and re-applied by `f` on the way out).
sites.responsiveScaling: follows planeSize.
sites.whatItSettles: The SDF's box half-extent, and the denominator of the rim colour's vertical gradient.

sites.formula: radius = min(cornerRadius, min(halfExtent.x, halfExtent.y)); q = abs(p) - halfExtent + radius; sdf = length(max(q, 0)) + min(max(q.x, q.y), 0) - radius
sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel space: the card's local XY multiplied by planeSize, so X and Y are world pixels on the card face and Z is the same pixel metric (the mesh scale (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1) is undone by this multiply and re-applied by `f` on the way out).
sites.responsiveScaling: through cornerRadius and halfExtent; sdf is in plane pixels and NEGATIVE inside the card.
sites.whatItSettles: The exact rounded-rectangle SDF. This is the single field the thickness profile, the rim band and the alpha cutout all read; the card's silhouette, its bevel and its rim cannot disagree because they are the same function.

sites.responsiveScaling: proportional to planeWidth, i.e. to the VIEWPORT, not to cardScale. 1440x900 -> 89.19 px; 390x844 -> 45.77 px; 844x390 -> 52.28 px.
sites.whatItSettles: cornerRadius is a fraction of the card WIDTH, capped at the half extent inside the SDF.

sites.formula: t = clamp(1 + sdf / max(bevelWidth, 0.001), 0, 1); p = max(bevelPower, 1); thickness(sdf) = pow(max(1 - pow(t, p), 0), 1/p) * thickness
sites.coordinateSpace: input sdf in plane pixels; output thickness in plane pixels.
sites.responsiveScaling: through bevelWidth (planeWidth) and thickness (cardScale).
sites.whatItSettles: A superellipse of the SDF: t = 1 at the card edge and 0 at bevelWidth inside. The profile is FLAT across the interior and turns over hard in the last few pixels -- the thickness derivative is 0 at the inner edge of the bevel band and diverges at the silhouette. That divergence, clamped, is the whole reflection support.

sites.responsiveScaling: proportional to planeWidth. 1440x900 -> 105.06 px; 390x844 -> 53.91 px; 844x390 -> 61.58 px.
sites.whatItSettles: The bevel BAND is wide (105 px at desktop). The reflective band is not the same thing as the bevel band: it is where the thickness gradient is large, which the superellipse power confines to the last few pixels.

sites.responsiveScaling: none -- a constant at every viewport.
sites.whatItSettles: The superellipse exponent. It is what makes a 105 px bevel band produce a few-pixel reflective band.

sites.responsiveScaling: proportional to cardScale (= planeWidth / referenceWidth*planeWidthRatio). 1440x900 -> 129.17 px; 390x844 -> 66.28 px; 844x390 -> 75.71 px.
sites.whatItSettles: The thickness AMPLITUDE. It scales with the card, so the thickness gradient -- thickness/bevelWidth -- is nearly viewport-invariant, and so is the bevel's normal profile.

sites.responsiveScaling: 6% of bevelWidth with a 0.35 px floor. 1440x900 -> 6.303 px; 390x844 -> 3.235 px; 844x390 -> 3.695 px. The floor only binds on a card narrower than ~30 px.
sites.whatItSettles: The gradient is NUMERIC, not analytic, and it is deliberately coarse -- a central difference over ~6 px at desktop. That is a low-pass on the normal: it is why the Target's bevel normal is smooth across the corners instead of ringing, and it must be reproduced at the same epsilon or the corner behaviour differs.

sites.formula: grad = vec2(T(p + (eps,0)) - T(p - (eps,0)), T(p + (0,eps)) - T(p - (0,eps))) / (2 * eps), where T(p) = thickness(sdf(p))
sites.coordinateSpace: plane pixels in, dimensionless slope out.
sites.responsiveScaling: through eps and through T; the slope itself is close to viewport-invariant.
sites.whatItSettles: Four extra SDF+thickness evaluations per fragment. The gradient is of the THICKNESS field, not of the SDF -- the bevel's slope, not the silhouette's direction.

sites.formula: slope = length(grad); g = grad * min(slope, bevelMaxSlope) / max(slope, 1e-4)
sites.responsiveScaling: none -- bevelMaxSlope is the constant 1.74 at every viewport.
sites.whatItSettles: The gradient is renormalised to at most bevelMaxSlope = 1.74, i.e. the bevel normal is never tilted past atan(1.74) = 60.1 degrees. Without this the divergence at the silhouette would tilt the normal to grazing and the fresnel would saturate on a sub-pixel ring.

sites.responsiveScaling: none.
sites.whatItSettles: The shipped clamp value.

sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel space: the card's local XY multiplied by planeSize, so X and Y are world pixels on the card face and Z is the same pixel metric (the mesh scale (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1) is undone by this multiply and re-applied by `f` on the way out).
sites.responsiveScaling: sphereRadius = contract sphereRadius (5000) * max(w,h)/referenceWidth -- the LAYOUT sphere, the same radius the grid places cards on.
sites.whatItSettles: The card is a section of the layout sphere, so its own curvature is the grid's curvature. Not a separate lens dome.

sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel space: the card's local XY multiplied by planeSize, so X and Y are world pixels on the card face and Z is the same pixel metric (the mesh scale (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1) is undone by this multiply and re-applied by `f` on the way out).
sites.responsiveScaling: |m| ~ |p| / sphereRadius; at a desktop card corner |p| ~ 342 px against sphereRadius 4167 px, so the sphere tilt is at most ~4.7 degrees.
sites.whatItSettles: The across-card tilt from the sphere bulge. It is ADDITIONAL to the rigid rotation that puts the card on the sphere (see cardPlacement): the card is rotated onto the sphere normal at its centre, and this term carries the normal's variation ACROSS the card face. Including both is not a double count.

sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel space: the card's local XY multiplied by planeSize, so X and Y are world pixels on the card face and Z is the same pixel metric (the mesh scale (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1) is undone by this multiply and re-applied by `f` on the way out). The Z component is the literal 1, which is what makes the XY slope-vs-1 ratio a tangent.
sites.responsiveScaling: none beyond its inputs.
sites.whatItSettles: ONE normal for the whole card: sphere tilt minus clamped bevel slope, in plane-pixel space, flipped for back faces. There is no second surface and no separate rim normal.

sites.formula: N *= faceDirection (three's gl_FrontFacing sign, +1 front / -1 back)
sites.responsiveScaling: none.
sites.whatItSettles: The plane is single-sided in practice (material side FrontSide) but the normal is still sign-corrected, so the law is orientation-safe.

sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel direction in, WORLD direction out.
sites.responsiveScaling: the /planeSize exactly cancels the mesh scale (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1), so `toWorld` is the card's pure ROTATION. That is what makes plane-space dot products equal world-space ones.
sites.whatItSettles: The bridge out of plane space, and the proof that dot(N, E) may be evaluated in EITHER space. Our card mesh carries a UNIFORM cardScale instead of a non-uniform plane scale, so the same cancellation gives normalize(modelWorldMatrix * vec4(N, 0)) -- identical rotation, not an analogue.

sites.formula: card.quaternion = rotation taking local +Z onto the sphere normal; card.scale = (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1)
sites.responsiveScaling: scale is the per-frame planeWidth / planeHeight.
sites.whatItSettles: The Target rigidly rotates each card onto its sphere normal AND bulges the plane within the card. Our engine does the same rigid rotation (setFromUnitVectors onto the slot normal), so carrying the sphere term across the card face is faithful rather than duplicated.

sites.coordinateSpace: sdf in plane pixels; rim dimensionless in [0, rimIntensity].
sites.responsiveScaling: through rimWidth (cardScale).
sites.whatItSettles: The rim is a band on the LAST rimWidth pixels of the SDF -- 0 at rimWidth inside, 1 at the silhouette. It rides the same field as the bevel and the cutout, so it cannot drift off the card edge. It is NOT a geometry attribute and NOT a fresnel term.

sites.responsiveScaling: proportional to cardScale. 1440x900 -> 8.333 px; 390x844 -> 4.276 px; 844x390 -> 4.884 px.
sites.whatItSettles: The rim band is EIGHT pixels wide at desktop -- an order of magnitude narrower than the 105 px bevel band, and narrower than our geometry rim.

sites.responsiveScaling: none.
sites.whatItSettles: The shipped rim amplitude, unchanged from O2.

sites.formula: f = saturate(p.y / max(halfExtent.y, 1e-4) * 0.5 + 0.5); rimColour = mix(rimColor, rimColorTop, f)
sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel space: the card's local XY multiplied by planeSize, so X and Y are world pixels on the card face and Z is the same pixel metric (the mesh scale (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1) is undone by this multiply and re-applied by `f` on the way out).
sites.responsiveScaling: normalised by halfExtent, so viewport-invariant.
sites.whatItSettles: A bottom-to-top rim colour ramp exists, but both endpoints are #ffffff in the shipped settings, so it is the identity. Recorded so a future round does not mistake a white rim for a missing feature.

sites.formula: schlick = F0 + (1 - F0) * pow(saturate(1 - dot(N, E)), 5)
sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel space -- and, because `toWorld` is a pure rotation, identically in world or view space.
sites.responsiveScaling: none.
sites.whatItSettles: The fresnel reads the ANALYTIC BEVEL NORMAL. This is the single most load-bearing fact of O3: the white reflection appears exactly where the bevel turns the normal, so the support field decides the band width.

sites.formula: Nw = toWorld(N); Ew = toWorld(E); reflected = normalize(reflect(-Ew, Nw))
sites.responsiveScaling: none.
sites.whatItSettles: The environment reflection is built from the SAME analytic normal, in world space, before the env rotations. One normal drives both the fresnel weight and the direction sampled -- they cannot disagree.

sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel space: the card's local XY multiplied by planeSize, so X and Y are world pixels on the card face and Z is the same pixel metric (the mesh scale (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1) is undone by this multiply and re-applied by `f` on the way out).
sites.responsiveScaling: none.
sites.whatItSettles: In the TARGET the same analytic normal also drives refraction. O3 is NOT AUTHORISED to change local refraction, so this site is recorded as a source fact and a deliberate, declared deviation: our refraction keeps its frozen O2 normal path. Any later round that wants refraction parity must open its own scope.

sites.formula: the complete shipped optics settings object
sites.responsiveScaling: the per-frame writes above turn these RATIOS into pixels: cornerRadius and bevelWidth by planeWidth, thickness and rimWidth by cardScale.
sites.whatItSettles: Every O3 constant in one place, unmodified since O0.

cardScale is the card's uniform scale against the reference card, and our SourceExactLayout computes it with the identical expression (planeWidth / REFERENCE_PLANE_WIDTH). thickness and rimWidth ride it; cornerRadius and bevelWidth do not.
The layout sphere radius the card's curvature term reads, and the same value our SourceExactLayout already computes for placement.

sites.formula: opacity = (1 - smoothstep(-w, w, sdf)) * materialOpacity, w = max(fwidth(sdf)*0.5, 1e-4)
sites.coordinateSpace: plane-pixel space: the card's local XY multiplied by planeSize, so X and Y are world pixels on the card face and Z is the same pixel metric (the mesh scale (planeWidth, planeHeight, 1) is undone by this multiply and re-applied by `f` on the way out).
sites.responsiveScaling: antialias width is screen-derived via fwidth.
sites.whatItSettles: The silhouette is the SAME SDF. Recorded because O3 must NOT touch it: our card silhouette is frozen geometry (superellipse n=5, radius 58 at TILE scale), so the O3 SDF drives ONLY the reflection support and the rim, never alpha or geometry.
